conbody.p: There is ongoing debate over whether the issue of copyright even warrants the creation of a separate small-claims court; that a tribunal that solely focuses on copyright is not necessary. A major factor to consider when addressing this concern, however, are the small-time copyright holders; the small business owners and independent artists who often face a difficult time financially when litigating violations of copyright. Oftentimes, in order to succeed creatively in this country, one must rely on the integrity of their original work. To be rid of a more accessible system would strip these small-time players of their right to a trial and ultimately their livelihood. With the ease the internet creates in committing copyright violations, and the rising prominence of MDJD litigation, there must be some measure put in place to make the process of copyright litigation more accessible, while still protecting defendants from financial exploitation. The CASE Act simply lowers the barrier for holders. While this is good for the small-time copyright holders, there are no measures in place to deter MDJD litigation and stop major holders from using the process to exploit defendants.
